key_insight: A longitudinal AI model identified elevated risk of future inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with median lead times of 20 months at UCSF and 15 months at an external safety-net hospital.
clinical_relevance: EHR-based risk identification could support research into earlier IBD detection, but whether it reduces diagnostic delay remains unproven.
method: Studied adults with IBD-compatible symptoms, signs, or findings in routine EHRs.
Trained Mamba and comparator models on pre-diagnostic data, excluding diagnostic-workup features.
Externally tested Mamba without recalibration and simulated diagnosis-code-only deployment.
evidence_signal: At the 6-month landmark among patients still undiagnosed, AUROC was 0.969 at UCSF and 0.965 externally; a separate deployment simulation reported 1.09% positive predictive value when reviewing 20 alerts per month.
watch_item: Low alert precision could create substantial review burden; prospective studies must establish clinical benefit before routine use.
paper_title: Prediction of incident inflammatory bowel disease from routine electronic health records: development and external validation of a longitudinal machine learning model
